samples.state_description: BPDA backbone hybrid diamine aerogel with 25% ODA fraction

characterizations.result_summary: All studied samples showed characteristic polyimide bands; BPDA backbone samples indicated complete imidization, while PMDA backbone samples showed signs of incomplete imidization.
Onset of decomposition of fabricated aerogels ranged from 422 °C to 621 °C.
Glass transition temperature in the range of 250 °C to 300 °C was observed for some samples.

evidence.source_sentence: Due to the sensitive relations between aerogel physical, thermal, and mechanical properties, improving the polyimide aerogels performance requires understanding of their structure to properties relations, along with introducing a robust method to tailor aerogels properties to achieve the optimum performance.

Given this background, this work extensively studies the structure to properties relations of pyromellitic dianhydride (PMDA) and biphenyl-tetracarboxylic acid dianhydride (BPDA) backbone polyimide aerogels at varying hybrid diamine fractions.
Based on the results, combination of rigid and flexible diamine monomers at varying fractions successfully tailored the properties of the hybrid diamine polyimide aerogels.
Keywords: Polyimide; Hybrid Aerogel; BPDA; PMDA; Mesoporous Solids;
As observed from Figure 3, increasing ODA diamine fraction on PMDA and BPDA backbone aerogels resulted in increased and decreased shrinkage, respectively.
However, the ODA-BPDA aerogels presented significantly lower shrinkage than PPDA-BPDAs.

Based on this, the higher shrinkage of BPDA backbone aerogels with increasing PPDA content is believed to be due to the greater chain rigidity, high planarity, and shorter chain length between cross-links of the PPDA-BPDA oligomers.<sup>13</sup> Such chain geometry allows the polymer chains to densely pack together.

Furthermore, the decreasing shrinkage of BPDA backbone aerogels with increasing ODA content is believed to be due to non-co-planarity of the ODA-BPDA oligomers due to existence of the oxygen linking groups between the phenyl rings.<sup>35,36</sup> The reduced shrinkage of PMDA backbone aerogels with increasing PPDA content is believed to be due to highly rigid nature of PPDA-PMDA bonding.<sup>20</sup>
However, due to the shorter chain length between the cross-links as well as the planarity of ODA-PMDA chains, addition of more flexible ODA monomers resulted in increased shrinkage.
Expressively, the BPDA backbone hybrid diamine aerogel with 25% ODA fraction (S7) presented even higher shrinkage than the PPDA-BPDA samples.

This suggests that at low ODA-BPDA content, rather than non-co-planarity and shorter crosslinks, the more flexible nature of ODA-BPDA chains plays the dominant role and as a result, increases the shrinkage.
As observed from Figure 3, except the PPDA-PMDA aerogels, the main shrinkage of the samples is occurred through the CO2 supercritical drying stage.

Furthermore, The PMDA backbone aerogels with ODA content of higher than 75% and The BPDA backbone aerogels with ODA content of less than 75%, presented high shrinkage ranging from 7% to 17% during the 24 h ageing stage.
Among the studied aerogels, PPDA-PMDA presented the lowest shrinkage of 7.3%, which is believed to be due to highly rigid and brittle nature of PPDA-PMDA bonding.<sup>20</sup>
As presented in Table 2, increasing the ODA content resulted in decreased and increased density of PMDA and BPDA backbone aerogels, respectively.
Among the studied aerogels, single diamine PPDA-PMDA and ODA-BPDA presented the lowest densities of 0.056 g/cm and 0.083 $\mathrm { g } / \mathrm { c m } ^ { 3 }$, correspondingly.
Similar to shrinkage results, it was observed that addition of 25% fraction of the diverse diamine monomer to dense PPDA-BPDA and ODA-PMDA aerogels did not affect the aerogels density considerably.
Roughly, similar morphology of the S3 and S5 as well as S6 and S7 aerogels is also in agreement with this observation.

From Figure 5A to Figure 5J, it is observed that the PMDA backbone aerogels fiber thickness, chain length between the crosslinks, and the average pore size were decreased with increasing ODA content.
Among the PMDA backbone aerogels, the S1 and S2 aerogels with PPDA content of more than 50% presented roughly similar morphology as well as fiber thickness of about 45 nm.
However, increasing the ODA content from 75% in sample S3 to 87.5% in sample S4 resulted in major pore size reduction, as presented in Figure 5F and Figure 5H.

As observed from Figure 5K to Figure 5T, the average pore size and particle diameter of the BPDA backbone aerogels were increased with increasing ODA content.<sup>13,17</sup> Furthermore, the increased pore size with increasing ODA fraction of BPDA backbone aerogels was commensurate with shrinkage and open cell content trends of those samples.
